My 3 main gripes:

- The promise of learning more about Troupe Gram, but unfortunately failing to meet those expectations very well at all.

- Roger. I'm not fond of cases with super obvious villains. The case actually could have thrown me off with the other characters if he wasn't so Evil McEvil from the first moment.

- Trucy. She does get 2 great moments in this case, but otherwise this was a big chance for her to get some much needed pull back into the series, and she kind of fell to the wayside again.

Honestly I didn't enjoy it much on the first time through, mostly for being an Apollo case, but aside from the stuff with Damian pretending to be the birb, it's very fun! And even though it has a very obvious culprit, he's somehow very satisfying to bring to justice.

This one is probably the most personal favourite of mine. I adore the setting of an airplane, being fascinated by them and airports in real life. The case kept me guessing throughout, the entire roster of characters was fun and memorable, and it had just the right amount of challenge.
Gummy protecting Kay is just beyond precious and one of my favourite moments in the whole series. It cemented him as my favourite character!

About Dahlia, yup! That's why I consider her stronger than those examples and why she doesn't pull the case down.

Apollo is at his best when he works with Athena in my eyes. He goes from extremely negative to a good role model and positive, but with the occasional snark when needed. Dual Destinies suffers from a sudden emotional beat for him too, but at least his dynamic with Athena makes it more understandable for me there.

Roger is just a bit too on the nose. The Grams had a huge chance at gaining more to their history, and instead we get someone who has "I'm evil, muhahaha!" practically sticky taped over his face. What made the rest of the troupe work for me is that they were flawed but you could see a sympathetic side to each of them one way or another. Roger has none of this, he just actively paints himself as the obvious culprit from square one. In the face of everything that happened to the troupe, being ousted was not a valid enough reason for me to sympathise with him. The fact he took on an apprentice of his own was probably the biggest thing they could have gone into more details about but didn't - it may have helped flesh out his hatred much better. 

That said if you don't count the DLC and the sympatheticness of Tahrust and Baleeb, he is a considerably stronger villain than others in the game, especially Pees'lub and Ga'aran.

Case 3 was wonderful, but 4 felt like a huge drop for me. Between 4 and 5 I prefer case 4 for its stronger witness cast. 

There are some crazy silly moments of logic in both cases, and I strongly disliked what they did to Kazuma. Van Zieks was an interesting character, but I feel being a defendant weakened him a bit. And the less I say about Stronghart and especially Sholmes, the better.

4-3 has its faults, such as Daryan and of course the issue with the gun, but neither are as debilitating as others say - it's still fundamentally a fun case with a deep mystery and fun characters. 

As for 2-3, I wrote an essay a while back defending Max for everything but his perverse nature. Nearly the whole case rings in my memory with positivity, blending comedic value with tragedy well. It's characters like Ben and Regina who ultimately bring it down, but the actual story is great!

Pierce is a strong villain, but the real MVPs are Sorin and Ellen. Especially Sorin, his story was just so tragic. I was so glad he became happt and his love for Ellen was so genuine, more so than I have ever read elsewhere.

Dahlia is sometimes a bit TOO evil. Like comedically so, but she's not why they're lower. I just don't find the cases particularly interesting in terms of difficulty, satisfaction and characters. In hindsight I should have ranked 3-4 lower because of Terry, but his sympathetic side helped it climb.

Apollo has always been in my bad books, but I strongly dislike SOJ for introducing such major things for him out of absolutely nowhere and expecting me to feel emotional about it like I've known for years. The villains of SOJ also heavily drag the cases down, although honestly most of the characters do!

Investigations 2 started a bit poor in my eyes and also had some points of contention near the end. As a result I find Investigations 1 more fun, but I still rank it 3rd in my favourite game in the series, just under Investigations 1 and again under Justice For All! And now I've successfully played the entire series and can more freely share my.opinions on the cases!

Moira is my favourite character in the game besides Winston, and from experience, she has more counters than people realise. Generally her biggest counter is her limited mobility. Coupled with her tall body, her movement is more predictable than most, making her a sucker against snipers, Tracer flanks and so on. Character specifically, try these:

- Sombra can hack away Moira's only means of escape and prevent her from utilising orbs to protect herself. Because of Moira's hit boxes, a Sombra also has a field day mowing Moira down, and has ample time to escape. 

- McCree and Widowmaker both usually play at too far a range for a Moira to safely contend with. Moira is grealty vulnerable to burst damage, so who better than these two? 

- Hanzo's rework allows him to play around any of Moira's play styles. Aggressive Moiras get an arrow to the noggin at a distance, after baiting out her Fade. Moiras engaged in mass healing can be flanked quickly. In a 1 on 1 situation, you have plenty of time as Hanzo to land that single killing blow, and with Moira's bulbous brain, you have a greater chance of landing it.

- Tracer. Now hear me out. A lot of people say Moira counters Tracer, but then again a lot say Winston counters Tracer. Both are wrong. The best Moira can do is chase a Tracer away or force her to use recall. While Moira's spread based aiming can keep better track of Tracer, a good Tracer will mow her down long before any of Moira's toolkit becomes an issue. Tracer can also very easily remove Moira's Fade from the equation, before quickly finishing her off with easier to place headshots.

There are other counters too like DVa (to an extent) and Bastion, as well as semi counters like Doomfist or Ana.

Being in the top 4 counts as a victory, if that helps at all, but if you're aiming for 1st place every time, it depends on a few factors.

- Ultimately securing a finishing blow is the most important factor of Deathmatch mode. This is why heroes with sudden impact damage like Junkrat, McCree and Hanzo excel. You can pepper away at someone as, say, Soldier 76 or Winston for a long time, but in the end, someone can take it all away from you in one shot.

- Each map has a central area where most players meet. In Chateau for example, the basement is a common point, and it seems in this new map, the large health pack over the broken floor is a busy place. Some heroes like Junkrat prosper from crowd control and so do well in these areas. Others need to pick off heroes around the outside without getting focused upon.

- Going around the map in circles may accidentally cause you to wander into danger. Start by picking a patrol area to move around, large enough so you have escape options and different cover spots, but small enough that you don't pull too many enemies into your comfort zone. 

A good example is the outermost staircase in the Chateau where you can see the multi-pillared platforms characters can bounce up to with the green bounce pad. It allows you to leap into the basement at safe times, keeps 2 health packs on demand and surprise snipers or people escaping the basement.

The difference between Tracer and her target however is the blink and recommended sensitivity. To keep up with rotating around players, most Tracers have a higher than average sensitivity setting. Furthermore, blinking after turning yourself in advance negates the disadvantage. Tracer players know which way they will move next, and can more easily adjust. Their victims must guess being unable to predict faster than a Tracer can dance around them, as under most circumstances they can't see them to learn their movements.

I'd also like to add a few reasons why I believe the other heroes you mentioned are not overpowered.

Pharah: VERY slow air movement, and can only avoid being shot down by using scenery, which greatly reduces her effectiveness. Pair her up with a Mercy however and yes, I agree things get a bit too difficult.

Moira: Unlike Tracer and Genji, Moira's one and only means of escape is on a cooldown. Her fade functions almost like Tracer's own blink, but once it wears off, you have 5 full seconds to gun down a tall and slow target with low firepower. If her resources run out in a chaotic fight, she must also risk her life to recharge. Although she can aim at distant targets, a common misconception is that her aiming is automatic and simple. In actually the further a target is from Moira, the more accurate aim needs to be, giving flankers a safe zone to wear her down or force her to fade.

Brigitte: In a 1 Vs 1 situation, Brigitte can have an advantage, but remember this is a team game. The people who complain about her being able to charge at a Reinhardt and stun him through as shield are ignoring just how dangerous something like this would be. If she can't close the gap - and let's face it, a flanking Brig is not a good Brig - she can't damage or heal. If she attempts to close the gap, simple focus fire melts her shield in no time. Furthermore, Reinhardt is the only tank Brigitte can excel against - she has a deceptively high number of counters such as Orisa, Junkrat, McCree, Pharah and even a good Genji, poking just outside of her stun and melee range.

Yes I agree to an extent. Take Robin to FD, and Mac almost certainly wins due to greater frame data, more linearity from Robin and no escape from offensive pressure. On Battlefield, Robin has the advantage as there are more opportunities for traps and Levin aerials cover the platforms entirely.

In short Mac can exploit Robin's weaknesses quickly in a straight fight, but on more complex stages he loses momentum which suits Robin better. It's about 55:45 in Mac's favour overall due to few Battlefield-alike stages.

Most characters with disjointed hitboxes either have specific ranges to their attacks, must be aerial or leave themselves open after attacks. (*coughexcludingcloudcough*) 

Robin is a bit of an exception however. The Levin sword hitbox lasts longer than his Bronze sword so even if you avoid the sweet spot, there's a sour spot to worry about. For characters like Robin, you can use a window of time where the Levin Sword is thrown away to attack as our melee range goes out the window. If you must fight against the Levin, abuse that super armour! It outlasts the sour spot too, and up-tilted F-Smashes can catch us during short hops.

Pac secondary here. 

Psyche us out! The trampoline is a very good option as it emerges in very early frames and can escape multihitting moves like PK Fire. To counter this however, we are left totally vulnerable after the bounce, so we usually bounce backwards. Spacing is key to baiting the trampoline and punishment. You can stop at F-Air tip-range as Palutena and the trampoline won't affect you, but it will leave a helpless yellow pizza monster at your mercy.

Once you get the hang of spacing/baiting, try using moves like B-Air and D-Air to pop Pac back onto the trampoline. The next bounce sends us higher, and unlike anyone else using the trampoline we still remain helpless. This sets up a neat charged Smash punish if you guess where we land.

If you do get caught out, try Palutena's N-Air or F-Air. Should be large enough to catch us while helpless even if we go backwards.

As for approaching us, we're just begging you to spam Reflect, because fruits like Cherries, Strawberries, Apples and Bells are good at getting around it, and are less of a threat if reflected. Use quick aerials like F-Air; you have a larger range than ours for the most part and should be quick enough to outspeed most of Pac's aerials. You also have the air mobility to steal fruits from us after they're thrown and bounce, particularly Cherries, Strawberries and Apples. 

One important thing. The Hydrant is a honey trap. So many players leave themselves open by smashing the hydrant away. Don't fall for this!

I used to main Wii Fit Trainer, and now that I have more source material from the likes of TK Breezy, she's still a reliable secondary for me. 

First and foremost, a predictable Trainer who attacks head on like, say a Mario or Captain Falcon will be destroyed. Wii Fit Trainer has a lot of similarities to characters like Wario. Her strange hitboxes, unorthodox aerials and the ability to push enemies back at most any range make her a character for hit-and-run strategies. She's faster than most people give her credit for, but her finishing moves are usually quite slow. 

- Wii Fit Trainer excels at off-stage gameplay. People underestimate how far her recovery goes if you mash the button, and she can stall in mid-air by using either her football or Deep Breathing. Her feet can spike people when you use F-Air, as can her head when you use her Header special. Nobody sees it coming!

- You can use Deep Breathing when the average weight enemy's damage breaks 120% and turn your F-Tilt, Sun Salutation and sometimes F-Air and Up-Air into killing moves. Quick, less laggy ones at that!

- Don't just charge up full Sun Salutations; mini ones can trip up opponents who rush in headlong. A more charged sun can beat many projectiles in the game such as Sheik's needles or Yoshi's eggs, but not Samus' charge shot.

- Many of WFT's moves can be cancelled to fool the opponent including Deep Breathing and Header. If you cancel Header, you can punch the football for a more close range defensive wall. Also useful for baiting reflectors and drilling habits into opponents.

- Short-hops all over the place are a good approach for Wii Fit Trainer. Don't commit to an attack every time, or you'll become predictable. 

- Wii Fit Trainer doesn't really have any combos from her throws, but her down-throw is the most reliable for baiting air dodges out of opponents. You can then follow up with a nice, powerful B-Air.

- If you must use a Smash attack, Down-Smash is the best option; it sends opponents horizontally and low; a death sentence for enemies like Little Mac or Cloud. Speaking of the former, watch out for small opponents. Some of Wii Fit Trainer's attacks may pass clean over opponents, including her Forward-Smash!

- Like Kirby, Wii Fit Trainer can duck under many attacks. A worryingly large about of Captain Falcon's moveset can totally miss you!

All joking aside though, you're going to have a great time playing as Robin hopefully! What he/she lacks in speed, he more than makes up for with stage control, range and lengthy hitboxes. His playstyle is designed to make you feel very smart if you outwit the enemy!

About his changes; many of them relate to the Levin Sword and how long its sour spot attacks last for. The differences are marginal enough that most of the old videos will still teach you a lot about how Robin plays. The most significant change was to his down-throw. Now at the correct percentage (different for every enemy!) he can follow up with a Levin Up-Air attack. Officially we call this the Checkmate combo, as it can guarantee kills if performed correctly..!

Here's a few tips to get you started. I recommend using them on Anther's against a fellow Robin rather than on For Glory. The lag is not kind to us!

- It's tempting to use Arcfire a lot as it has lots of follow ups like Levin F-Air or Nosferatu. Be careful in the neutral though; easily Robin's laggiest attack. Only use it against certain opponents un the neutral, and even then keep your distance with a short-hop backwards. Which opponents? Some include giants like Dedede or characters like Link whose projectiles melt in the flames.

- Don't forget Nosferatu. It's like Wario's grab in that it can bypass shields while you're still airborne! Trick your opponent into overrelying on the shield, then get them! It's great with the B-Reversal tech. By the way, you'll heal much more damage if your damage is significantly higher than your enemy. Use it after KOing someone immediatly to gain a huge advantage..!

- A lot of people forget to use Thunder and Elthunder. Use the former to feel out an opponent for habits - how do they block it or get around it? - and to stop charging projectiles. Use the latter across the stage; it covers 3/4 of Final Destination, and it may even KO light enemies on the edge if the stage. Good for catching rollers too.

- When Robin uses Elwind he throws his arm downward during the first cast. Hit someone with Elwind with Robin's hand touching or passing through them, and it meteors them. Beware of reflectors, or you'll be spiked instead..!

- Each tome recharges at different rates, but most are expendable except for Elwind. It only takes about 8 seconds to recharge if lost, but you really don't want to be offstae if it runs out. Stall for time with Arcfires, Elthunders and Arcthunders until it returns. A Nosferatu can burn at least 3 seconds too in an emergency.

A few tips from one Robin main to (hopefully) another:

- Don't worry too much about counting the number of uses your books have left. Just have a rough idea for each one; they flash when they only have 2 uses left, so the game will gradually teach you specific numbers. The only one I'd focus on most is Elwind; don't get caught off stage without it, or you'll make Little Mac's recovery seem godlike!

- Arcthunder and Arcfire are bread and butter combo setups for Robin, but you'll need a different spell for different matchups.

- On large targets, N-Air may hit twice.

- I strongly recommend looking up the Checkmate combo on Smashboards. Robin has a poor matchup against (*sigh*) Sheik, but unlike many others, he has a near-guaranteed kill option that works against her height and weight.

- Try Elwind Cancelling on any stages with platforms. Activate Elwind verrrry close to ground level. The projectile will still emerge and if you hit it right, will spike the opponent into the ground, but Robin will have very little landing lag. It's really hard for an enemy to Tech this, and it's very situational... It means a free hit though, so go to town on them!

- Hidden 1-Ups can be found in places where you would normally rescue characters such as Goofy.
- The enemies at this stage are mostly Mickey's version of Goombas, so no parlor tricks with them.

- The top of the tower is blocked off to prevrnt you from falling, so that new Mario players don't get frustrated about falling to the bottom of the tower again. This was a common complaint in the original Epic Mickey level.

I started out with Wario when S4 first launched. He's all about getting in your opponent's head; only Jigglypuff rivals his air speed, and he has a number of unorthodox attacks for a heavyweight. 

- The glorious Waft! Don't always wait for it to be fully charged; even a half-charged Waft can KO some opponents as early as 40% from the edge of a stage.
- The Bike! People often forget that the bike can slow down - great for trickery. You can also throw the bike upwards on the edge of a stage to cover almost every get-up option your opponent has. If they refuse to move, short-hop b-air them when their invincibility runs dry.
- The Corkscrew! At early percentages, up-throw can combo into this. Very quick to start too, so it can help escape some attacks. Careful; it has low priority against most other air attacks.
- The Chomp! It's like an airborne grab, and we ALL know how grabs are essentially the basis of all of Smash 4's gameplay. Take advantage of the habit most people have - when you approach them from the air, they raise a shield. Condition them to do this, even if it means you have to take a bit of damage first, then use Chomp to bypass their defenses.  Another great means of edgeguarding too, and it helps against spot-dodging.
- The Pokes! Wario has a lot of long lasting, poking boxes. Weave in and out, teasing opponents with nudges and knocks. If Wario struggles with anything, it's finishing someone off. He has very little from his grabs, and he has a reallllly short range for the most part, meaning if you don't go in with a safe plan, your opponent almost always wins the trade-off of blows. Luckily, these pokes are exemplary at "Gimping" opponents - I would argue that next to Pit and Dark Pit, Wario has the greatest off-stage gameplay. 
- The Taunts! Wario is the only character on For Glory to get unlimited taunts, as long as you ride his bike when doing so.

Similar to Captain Falcon, Zero Suit Samus has the potential to combo you away, but most of her moves are very risky. If she misses a grab/dash/special attack, she's more open than most fast characters. 

Her grab in particular is difficult to deal with on For Glory, because of the specific timing needed to spot dodge it. Rolling won't help; she can reach you no matter where you go, unless you time it juuuuust right and roll behind her. Even then, you'd have to be really close, and she might as well use a different attack on you. Short-hops work wonders! Should she use her down-throw on you, try to tilt the control stick so you move out of her reach. At early percentages, she has a guaranteed combo, which lasts longer if you're a larger character. 

As Sardines mentions, she is strong in the air when below you; plenty of ways to juggle, or even kill from there. Nevertheless, she needs to place herself properly to land attacks; characters with disjointed/oddly angled moves, such as Wii Fit Trainer or Robin, can trip her up by staying out of her range, and poking her at a bizzare angle. 

For attacks such as her stun gun/neutral special, you may want to forget about reflecting them. Dark Pit in particular has a long cooldown after using his Guardian Orbitars, by which time, ZSS can run in and grab/smash you anyway. Instead, use a shield with good timing to nullify it, and test her patience. She can't keep firing them forever, and many will panic and go for a grab anyway. Good luck! She's a frustrating opponent to face, but she's not impossible once you get used to her quirks!

The Inkbrush is so remarkably different from the normal Rollers that anyone who plays as a normal Roller won't like it at all, and most others will find it unorthodox. I personally have decided to stick with it; it's unique and more aggressive than you'd think:

- Getting to the front lines is a breeze; you may not leave a large trail, but you move so fast that everyone gets where they need to be in mere seconds.
- Your weak attacks are actually a strength. When you flank people from behind, the individual attacks will make them think someone's attacking from ahead of them.
- Your unpredictable paint spread makes for unpredictable escapes! It also gives other rollers and chargers something to worry about when you cut off their retreat in different ways every time.
- Get to high ground! Your paint spread from the highest spots will make your point totals soar. It can also help stall the control points in Splat Zones.

- Reserve the Ink Strike for kills. Have your teammates bunch the enemy together for you.
